entries.test: Public controlled experiments separating textual word associations from real-world relationships would show whether semantic-leakage errors track the former rather than the latter.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supports restricting the proposition to these kinds of errors. The probabilistic parenthetical examples do not hedge the main assertion.

entries.test: Public controlled fine-tuning experiments would show whether training on number sequences from a preference-conditioned model induces corresponding preferences in another model.
entries.note: In context, “bend it to your will” refers to demonstrated preference transfer. This asserts a causal capability, not a probabilistic future possibility.
Neither putting society “in the hands” of LLMs nor “not going to end well” supplies a shared criterion for testing the prediction.
